title: Former State Minister Anupa Pasquel’s salary, allowances, expenditure examined in court
byline: Evidence concerning the income, salary, allowances, bank accounts and expenditure of former State Minister Anupa Pasquel has been recorded before the Colombo High Court in a case filed by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC).

title: Police open fire at three-wheeler in Borella
byline: A three-wheeler came under police fire in the Veluwana area of Borella after its occupants allegedly ignored orders to stop, police said.

title: US pounds Iran, Tehran strikes back at bases in biggest exchange since July
byline: Iranians and their Arab neighbours feared a return of war on Wednesday after the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington ​since July, with U.S. forces striking Iran’s southern coast and Iran firing at American bases across the region.

title: PM holds bilateral talks with Bhutanese counterpart
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya held bilateral talks with Bhutanese Prime Minister Dasho Tshering Tobgay in Thimphu during her visit to Bhutan to deliver the keynote address at the inaugural Global Conscious Food Systems Summit 2026.

title: 250 Ceylon King Coconut Villages to be established
byline: A national programme to establish 250 “Ceylon King Coconut Villages” across Sri Lanka over the next three years was launched today (2) at the Coconut Cultivation Board’s Mahayaya Estate in Kurunegala.

title: Polonnaruwa records Sri Lanka’s highest temperature at 37.9°C
byline: Polonnaruwa recorded country’s highest maximum temperature of 37.9°C today (September 2), to the Meteorology Department said.

title: CSE slips as late selling drags ASPI lower
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange reversed Monday’s marginal gains on Tuesday, 1 September 2026, with both benchmark indices closing lower as selling pressure strengthened during the latter part of the session.

title: Trade unions oppose EPF, ETF move
byline: Independent trade unions and multi-society organisations staged a leaflet distribution campaign on September 2 at 5 p.m. to raise concerns over a proposal to remove the Employees’ Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees’ Trust Fund (ETF) from the control of the Central Bank of Sri Lanka and place them under the management of a three-member committee.

title: Public invited to name Dehiwala Zoo’s baby hippo
byline: Animal lovers have been given an opportunity to suggest a name for a baby Nile hippopotamus recently born at the Dehiwala National Zoo.

title: Venues, dates confirmed for inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy
byline: The first-ever edition of the ICC Women’s Champions Trophy will take place from February 14 to 28 in India next year.

title: Parliament to debate Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill on September 9
byline: The Sectoral Oversight Committee on Governance, Justice and Civil Protection has approved the Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) Bill, which is scheduled to be debated in Parliament on September 9 for its Second Reading.

title: Kurunegala student tops Grade 5 Scholarship exam with 193 marks
byline: A student from the Kurunegala District has secured the highest mark of 193 in the 2026 Grade 5 Scholarship Examination in the Sinhala medium, Commissioner General of Examinations A.K.S. Indika Kumari Liyanage said.

title: Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath undertakes official visit to UAE
byline: Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Minister Vijitha Herath will undertake an official visit to the United Arab Emirates from September 2 to 3, 2026.

title: Strict action against bullying children over grade 5 results
byline: The Women and Child Affairs Ministry has warned that strict legal action will be taken against anyone who punishes or mentally harasses children based on their Grade 5 Scholarship Examination results.

title: MoU signed for technology to prevent wild elephant-train collisions
byline: A Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed yesterday (September 1) to introduce a technological system aimed at preventing wild elephants from being killed in train collisions.

title: Colombo water supply to be suspended for 24 hours
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) has announced a 24-hour suspension of the water supply in several areas of Colombo due to essential maintenance work at the Ambatale Water Treatment Plant.

title: Japan donates seven buses to Sri Lanka
byline: Japan has donated seven low-floor buses to Sri Lanka to support the development of public transport services, under the ongoing development cooperation between the two countries.

title: Grade 5 Scholarship Examination 2026 results released
byline: The results of the 2026 Grade 5 Scholarship Examination, held on August 9, have been released today (September 2), the Examinations Department said.

title: Yala solar-powered water system remains operational: Wildlife Department
byline: The Wildlife Conservation Department has denied reports that the solar-powered water supply system at Yala National Park has been deactivated, saying the park’s main water pipeline system remains operational and is continuously supplying water to wildlife.

title: Vehicle registrations dip in July as inventory buildup obscures true credit demand
byline: Total motor vehicle registrations across Sri Lanka moderated to 53,221 units in July 2026, down from 58,151 units in June.

title: Sri Lanka launches National Food Safety Policy
byline: Sri Lanka has launched its National Food Safety Policy, marking a major step towards strengthening food safety governance, protecting public health and building safer, healthier and more resilient agrifood systems.

title: Complaint lodged with CIABOC against all NPP MPs
byline: A complaint has been lodged against all 159 National People’s Power (NPP) MPs and officials in charge of NPP and Janatha Vimkuthi Peramuna (JVP) with the Commission to Inquire Allegations against Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) by Nidahas Satan Madyastanaya yesterday.

title: Government ready to face referendum if required: Nalinda
byline: Cabinet Spokesman Minister Nalinda Jayatissa reiterated that the Government would hold a referendum if the Supreme Court rules that the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution requires approval through a referendum.

title: BIA welcomes travellers with authentic Ceylon Tea
byline: Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) has been promoting Sri Lanka’s renowned Ceylon Tea as part of its efforts to offer travellers a warm and authentic Sri Lankan welcome.

title: Robert Kiyosaki, the ‘Rich Dad Poor Dad’ author, is $1.2 billion in debt
byline: Robert Kiyosaki, author of ’Rich Dad Poor Dad,’ owes $1.2 billion, and he says that’s a feature, not a bug. He’s made a career out of teaching people that debt doesn’t have to be a financial disaster. In fact, he’s very public about the staggering amount he owes, explaining that debt, when used right, is core to how he built wealth.

title: 5,000 solar technicians needed annually to meet 2030 renewable energy target: PUCSL
byline: Sri Lanka needs to produce around 5,000 qualified solar power technicians annually to support the installation of approximately 600 megawatts of solar power capacity each year and achieve its target of generating 70% of electricity from renewable sources by 2030, Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) Chairman Prof. K.P.L. Chandralal said.

title: SC commences hearing petitions on Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill
byline: The Supreme Court a short while ago commenced its hearing into 14 Special Determination petition filed challenging the Constitutionality of the Anti-Corruption (Amendment) Bill.

title: Vehicle prices increase by millions
byline: Vehicle prices in Sri Lanka have begun increasing sharply, with some popular models seeing increases of up to Rs. 4.5 million, following the Government’s decision to extend a 50% surcharge on vehicle import duties until December 31.

title: AG tells SC 22nd Amendment does not require referendum
byline: The Attorney General yesterday informed the Supreme Court that the proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution does not seek to amend any of the entrenched provisions specified in Article 83 of the Constitution and, therefore, does not require approval at a referendum.

title: Wildlife Department hunts suspect over alleged Yala poaching
byline: The Department of Wildlife Conservation has launched a probe to apprehend a man allegedly involved in poaching inside Block V of Yala National Park, after a video capturing the incident was handed over to wildlife officials.

title: Foreign tourist gets sex invitations under hotel door
byline: Three Sri lankan men were arrested by the Unawatuna Tourist Police after allegedly slipping written invitations under the room door of a 63-year-old Australian woman’ inviting her to engage in sexual activity with them.

title: Dutch shift 86 tonnes of gold from US and Canada to UK
byline: The Dutch central bank said on Wednesday that it had moved 86 tonnes of its gold reserves out of the United States and Canada to London, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest”.

title: Iranian Vessels: U.S. embassy says no comment on private diplomatic communications
byline: In response to a question whether the U.S. had any communication with the Sri Lankan authorities over the Iranian vessels anchored off the coast of Sri Lanka, an embassy spokesperson said that the substance of private diplomatic conversations would not be commented on

title: Air Vice Marshal Indika Wickramasinghe assumes duties as KDU Vice Chancellor
byline: Air Vice Marshal Indika Wickramasinghe assumed duties as the new Vice Chancellor of the General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University (KDU).

title: Sri Lanka loses over USD 20 MN as ICC moves Champions Trophy to India
byline: Despite the Sri Lanka Cricket Transformation Committee having remained hopeful that it could have convinced the International Cricket Council (ICC) to keep the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy in Sri Lanka, the country has now lost the hosting rights for the tournament, with the ICC confirming India as the replacement host.

title: Veteran artist and animation pioneer Givantha Arthasad dies at 73
byline: Veteran artist and film technician Givantha Arthasad, who created Sri Lanka’s first animated cartoon film, has passed away at the age of 73.

title: Heat index expected to reach ‘Caution’ level in several areas
byline: The heat index, which indicates the temperature felt by the human body, is expected to rise to the ‘Caution’ level in several parts of the country during the daytime.

title: Rs. 3 billion allocated for compensation over drought-hit crops
byline: The Government has allocated Rs. 3 billion to provide agricultural insurance compensation to farmers whose crops have been damaged by drought conditions associated with El Niño.

title: Police told not to issue charges for missing digital insurance cards
byline: Traffic police officers have been instructed not to issue charge sheets to motorists solely for failing to produce a digital vehicle insurance card, Deputy Inspector General of Police (DIG) in charge of the Traffic Control and Road Safety Range W.P.J. Senadheera said.

title: Sri Lanka Women secure automatic qualification for 2027 Champions Trophy
byline: Sri Lanka’s women’s national cricket team has secured automatic qualification for the inaugural ICC Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027, Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) announced.

title: Two suspects deported from Abu Dhabi over drugs, firearms and organised crime
byline: Two Sri Lankan suspects wanted for investigations into drugs, illegal possession of firearms and organised crime have been deported from Abu Dhabi and handed over to Sri Lankan authorities.

title: UNICEF estimates 20 million children suffered online sexual abuse in one year
byline: About 20 million internet-using children across ​21 countries were subjected to sexual exploitation or abuse on digital platforms in a single year, with most cases occurring ‌on social media platforms, a new report by the U.N. children’s charity said on Thursday.

title: NVQ to be mandatory for refrigeration, air-conditioning technicians
byline: National Vocational Qualification (NVQ) certification will become mandatory for refrigeration, air-conditioning and vehicle air-conditioning technicians under new rules issued by the Sri Lanka Engineering Council.

title: US warns EB-1 green cards may shut for India
byline: The United States has warned that employment-based first-preference green cards for Indians could become unavailable within weeks because of heavy demand, adding fresh pressure to an already severe backlog that has left another major category closed to Indian applicants.

title: El Niño set to become very strong, raising risks of extreme weather into 2027
byline: El Niño is firmly established and will intensify into a very strong event in the coming months, with big impacts on rainfall and temperature patterns and associated risks of floods, drought and extreme heat, according to a new update from the World Meteorological Organization (WMO).

title: Sri Lanka, India move to finalise MoU for Kankesanthurai Port development
byline: Sri Lanka and India have taken steps to expedite the finalisation of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the development of the Kankesanthurai Port with Indian Government support.

title: Wild elephant hits bus carrying pilgrims in Buttala; 10 injured
byline: A private bus carrying a group of pilgrims returning from Kataragama veered off the road and overturned after a wild elephant obstructed its path and struck the vehicle in the Buttala area.

title: President’s Secretary calls for urgent relief from PAYE Tax burden
byline: Secretary to the President Dr. Nandika Sanath Kumanayake has called for immediate measures to ease the heavy Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) tax burden on the general public, stressing that the current situation requires swift corrective action.

title: Petrol cars below 1,000cc top vehicle imports in 2026
byline: Petrol cars with engine capacities below 1,000cc accounted for the highest customs revenue among vehicle imports in 2026, generating Rs. 137.4 billion, officials informed the Committee on Ways and Means.

title: Mystery deepens over Eraj Fernando’s death
byline: An open verdict has been returned following the post-mortem examination into the death of former Hambantota Mayor Eraj Fernando.

title: New Court of Appeal Judge Sajeewani Dilka Lakmali sworn in
byline: Sajeewani Dilka Lakmali Karunannayake was sworn in as a Judge of the Court of Appeal before President Anura Kumara Dissanayake at the Presidential Secretariat this afternoon (3).

title: Apple facing $2.7 billion UK lawsuit over ’unfair’ app tracking rules
byline: Apple (AAPL.O), is facing a £2 billion ($2.7 billion) London lawsuit brought on behalf of app developers over its app tracking rules, with the ​iPhone maker accused of abusing its power to unfairly impose ‌greater restrictions on third parties.

title: Online applications planned for 2027 Grade 6 school admissions
byline: Parents of students who sat the 2026 Grade 5 Scholarship Examination will have to await further instructions on the online application process for Grade 6 school admissions in 2027.

title: Forced labour programme helped cut US tariffs to 10%: Deputy Minister
byline: The programme to eliminate forced labour in Sri Lanka was a reason for the reduction of US tariffs on Sri Lankan exports from 12.5% to 10%, Deputy Minister of Labour Mahinda Jayasinghe said.

title: Ex-ambassador praises efficient passport service
byline: Former Sri Lankan Ambassador to the United States, Mexico and Trinidad and Tobago Mahinda Samarasinghe has praised the staff at Sri Lanka’s Passport Office for their helpful and efficient service.

title: CSE builds momentum as broad-based buying lifts both indices
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange extended its positive momentum on Thursday, 3 September 2026, with both benchmark indices closing higher as buying interest strengthened across the broader market.

title: Toxic wildfire haze spreads across South East Asia as ’super’ El Niño intensifies
byline: A blanket of toxic haze is enveloping parts of Indonesia and spreading into Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines, as weeks-long wildfires continue to burn.

title: Dudley Sirisena spends Rs. 3.5 mn to renovate Polonnaruwa Railway Station
byline: Sri Lankan businessman Dudley Sirisena said he had spent Rs. 3.5 million to renovate the Polonnaruwa Railway Station and pledged to maintain the station at his own expense for one year.

title: School dropouts eligible for truck-driving jobs in Japan
byline: School dropouts will also have the opportunity to apply for certain jobs in Japan, including truck-driving positions, provided they have the required Japanese language proficiency, Sri Lanka Foreign Employment Agency (SLFEA) Chairman  Lal Hettiarachchi said.

title: Kennedy asked to remove Pennsylvania measles death from CDC tally, sources say
byline: U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. asked his new CDC director to remove a reference to two Pennsylvania deaths from the agency’s online measles tally after he questioned whether the disease contributed to the ​fatalities, three sources familiar with the situation said.

title: Dayasiri urges Polls Commission  to intervene and stop SLFP event today
byline: MP Dayasiri Jayasekera today urged the Elections Commission to intervene and stop an event which has been organised by the Nimal Siripala group to mark the 75th anniversary of the Sri Lanka Freedom Party (SLFP) today.

title: 40 buses fail inspection in Pettah
byline: Around 40 inter-provincial private and Sri Lanka Transport Board (SLTB) buses were found to have failed to meet the required standards during a special inspection in Pettah today (03).

title: Sumanthiran’s post on natural justice sparks social media interest
byline: Former TNA Parliamentarian and President’s Counsel M.A. Sumanthiran has drawn public attention on social media after posting two Latin legal maxims relating to the fundamental principles of natural justice: that no one should be a judge in their own case and that the other side should also be heard.

title: ‘Become un-purchasable or leave the uniform’: President warns corrupt Police
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has issued a stern warning to police officers colluding with drug traffickers and organised criminal groups, telling them to overcome their fear, remain beyond the reach of criminals or leave the police service.

title: UN Human Rights Office calls on Govt to bolster accountability
byline: UN Human Rights spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said that the UN Human Rights Office calls on the Sri Lankan Government to build on the steps it has taken to bolster accountability for human rights violations and to advance reconciliation and healing.

title: Time to build a respected Police force: President
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said that steps would be taken to provide the necessary facilities to transform the Sri Lanka Police into a highly respected service. He said a proper promotion scheme would be introduced, a new uniform is expected to be provided by around the middle of next year and measures would be taken to provide all police officers with a risk allowance,

title: Three Colombo rail routes to get electric trains
byline: Construction of Sri Lanka’s long-awaited electric railway network is expected to commence by May or June next year, Transport, Highways and Urban Development Minister Bimal Rathnayaka said.

title: Botham recovers after first-of-its-kind cancer surgery
byline: Dehiwala Zoo’s beloved sea lion “Botham” is recovering well following a special cancer surgery described as the first of its kind in Sri Lanka, zoo officials said.

title: Public urged to avoid flying kites near high-voltage lines
byline: The National System Operator (NSO) has urged the public to avoid flying kites underneath or near 220 kV and 132 kV high-voltage transmission lines, towers and grid substations.

title: 22nd Amendment hearing: BASL skips written submissions after denial of oral reply
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL), by filing a motion before the Supreme Court today, informed that it will not be tendering the post-hearing written submissions in connection with its Special Determination applications, citing circumstances including the court’s decision to refuse the petitioners an oral right of reply after the Attorney General’s oral submissions during last Wednesday’s (2) hearings.
